# Grid keyboard navigation ends on c12, not c3, after twelve ArrowLeft inputs

## Context

`test/playwright/e2e/grid/KeyboardNavigationScroll.spec.mjs` (the arm #18871 / PR #18873 introduced: arrowing right past the visible columns and back left keeps the selected cell rendered and visible) has now gone red on CI twice with the same shape, with no test or source change that explains it:

| when | where | observed |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-09-18 | a CI shard of the cell-editing day (recorded on #18910 and #18919 as "tracked separately" — it never was, this ticket is that follow-up) | the first poll saw `{inside: false, text: 'r3c15'}`; locally under `--workers=10 --repeat-each=30` the arm ended STUCK on `{inside: false, text: 'r3c12'}` once in 30; a state-dumping probe over 130 further runs never reproduced it. **Unclassified.** |
| 2026-10-09 | PR #19509 at `c3e55797840904a3c644ecc20334ae83779aa452`, run 37958019884 attempt 1, job 113913447127 (@neo-gpt-sophie's receipt: https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19509#issuecomment-6084797298) | line 61: expected `{inside: true, text: 'r3c3'}`, got `{inside: false, text: 'r3c12'}`; the trace records twelve ArrowRight then twelve ArrowLeft; the right terminal `r3c15` was correct, the left terminal stayed `r3c12` through the whole 5 s poll; the final grid View is active; 69 other tests of the shard passed; the arm is 5/5 locally at that head and at the preceding 828712fc5f (Node 24.19, headless branded Chrome, macOS); the requested rerun went green. **Narrowed (Sophie, the retained trace's frame snapshots, https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19515#issuecomment-6085142673):** the terminal DOM holds TWO selected cells — pooled slot `__row-2__cell-0` = c12 (`neo-selected`, `aria-selected="true"`, left 1650 px; stale since the ArrowLeft at call 1850, where c12 and c11 were both selected) and slot `__row-2__cell-2` = c3 (selected, left 300 px) — with the body's `--grid-scroll-left` ended at 300 px (down from 1150 px). The spec's first-match read returned the stale c12: "the navigation never reached c3" is disproved for this occurrence, which points at the second producer below (a stale projection); whether the extra class originates in the row's vdom, its adopted vnode or Main's applied deltas is open — the trace carries no worker-side state. |

Sophie retains today's trace (artifact 11630205953) and a diagnostic witness. A green rerun is not causal proof; neither occurrence captured worker-side selection state, so the producer is OPEN, not classified. Her bounded probes at `c3e5579784` (terminal-state dumps 30/30, CPU throttling ×4 15/15, a controlled late-selection race 8/8, a scroll/recycling crossing 2/2 — receipts in the comment above) did not reproduce the failure and prove nothing harmless.

## The Problem

Three producers fit both sightings and nothing in the recorded evidence tells them apart:

1. **lost input** — keydowns dropped or coalesced under shard load (three ArrowLeft of twelve would leave c15 → c12);
2. **stale selection projection** — the model is on c3 but a `.neo-selected` class still sits on a pooled cell: the spec's `selectedCell()` reads `querySelector` of the selected-cell selector, the first match in DOM order, and pooled cells are not in column order;
3. **a skipped scroll** — `scrollByColumns` declines because `body.scrollLeft` trails the requested scroll (the unmeasured note on #18873), so the selected cell is correct in the model but outside the visible width.

The October occurrence is narrowed toward the second (the two-selected-cells terminal DOM above); the September occurrence remains unclassified against all three. Only the third is a scroll defect; the first is an input-path defect; the second is a projection defect that any keyboard user of a pooled grid would see as a wrong highlight. The arm's assertion is the user-facing contract from #18871 and must stay as it is — no per-key waits to green it, and no read that picks the other selected node.

## The Architectural Reality

`Neo.selection.grid.CellModel#onNavKeyColumn` is purely logical (model and selection only). `Neo.grid.Container#scrollByColumns` (rewritten geometrically in #18873: visible width = container width minus the scrollbar bands, position by `dataField`, locked columns skipped) issues the scroll; `Neo.grid.Body#afterSetScrollLeft` recomputes the column window; the body pools cells across scrolls, so the DOM order of cells is the pool's, not the columns'. The spec's `selectedCell(page)` and `scrollLeft(page)` helpers read the DOM in the real browser; the trace carries every key event and the final DOM, no worker state.

Design authority: not applicable — a red assertion against the arm's own contract, no behavior is called wrong here.

## The Fix

1. Reproduce under the same conditions (`--workers=10 --repeat-each=30`, the full grid e2e shard beside it) with a worker-state probe aligned to the complete arrow sequence: `selectionModel.items`, the selected row's vdom, the adopted vnode, and Main's selected-cell classes — collected inside the event path or asynchronously at the terminal, never by awaiting a worker read after each key (that changes the timing under diagnosis); a per-key `scrollLeft` read beside it separates producer 3 from the others.
2. Classify (lost input / stale projection / skipped scroll) from the fingerprint, then repair in the owning layer: the key path, the selection projection's class bookkeeping on pooled cells, or `scrollByColumns`' read of the current scroll position.
3. Keep the arm; add the producer's own arm so the mechanism cannot return silently.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The producer is named on this ticket from a reproduction with worker-side state, not inferred from the DOM alone.
- [ ] The repair lands in the owning layer with an arm that reds on the producer and greens on the fix.
- [ ] `KeyboardNavigationScroll.spec.mjs` unchanged in its assertions, green 30/30 locally under `--workers=10 --repeat-each=30` and on the next three CI runs touching the grid shard.

## Out of Scope

The cell-editing arms and the text-field trailing-space defect (#18910, fixed); any per-key wait or retry inside the arm.

## Related

### Existing failed trace: the final DOM has two selected cells

I reconstructed the incremental frame snapshots from retained artifact **11630205953**, `grid-KeyboardNavigationScr-8c370-d-cell-rendered-and-visible-chromium/trace.zip`. Decoder follows the installed Playwright `snapshotNodes` post-order indexing and `SnapshotRenderer` back-reference resolution; no new browser run or changed input sequence.

At `call@1850`, action snapshot (94148.908 ms), `__row-2__cell-0` still renders **c12**, `neo-selected`, `aria-selected=true`, while `__cell-10` renders **c11** with the same selected flags. The stale c12 then survives successive selection changes. By `call@1864` before-snapshot (94356.418 ms), and still at final `call@1876` after-snapshot (99156.180 ms), the row contains:

| Slot | data-field / text | class | aria-selected | left |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `neo-grid-body-4__row-2__cell-0` | c12 / r3c12 | neo-grid-cell neo-selected | true | 1650px |
| `neo-grid-body-4__row-2__cell-2` | c3 / r3c3 | neo-grid-cell neo-selected | true | 300px |

The center body's `--grid-scroll-left` ends at **300px**, down from 1150px. Thus the first selected node being c12 is a **stale extra selected DOM cell**, not proof that the navigation stopped at c12. The original test correctly rejects that visible state; do not change it to choose the other selected node.

This narrows the current occurrence toward projection. It still does not tell us whether the extra class originates in row VDOM, its adopted vnode, or Main's applied deltas; the trace has no worker-state read. That is the next discriminator. The September occurrence remains separately unclassified.

### Bounded diagnostic results (source `c3e5579784`)

Playwright's own `SnapshotStorage` / `SnapshotRenderer` independently reproduces the final c12+c3 selected pair above.

- Original key sequence, terminal-only model/VDOM/vnode/Main dump: **30/30 pass**, 10 workers, 44.2 s. Every dump has only c3 selected on all four surfaces, scrollLeft 300, and no pending/in-flight row update.
- Same sequence with CDP browser CPU throttling at rate 4: **15/15 pass**, 5 workers, 34.9 s; the same four-surface result.
- Controlled late-selection discriminator: **8/8 pass**, 9.8 s. A grid/View/body/row `beforeExecuteVdomUpdate` hook issues one or nine left selections only after that owner's payload is collected, using the real browser pipeline. The four one-step cases end consistently at c11; the four nine-step cases at c3. This is a controlled race hypothesis, not a reproduction of the original input sequence.

Run IDs: `sophie-19515-terminal-state`, `sophie-19515-terminal-state-cpu4`, `sophie-19515-captured-flight`. Temporary observations and controls were saved as a diagnostic patch and removed from the tracked spec; the original assertions and source are unchanged. These negative probes do not close the issue or prove the initial failure harmless. The next discriminator is selection/row recycling and batch adoption together; a peer challenge has gone to the original investigator.

### Peer-proposed scroll/recycling crossing

A further **2/2 browser control** passed (run `sophie-19515-row-scroll-cross`, 8.3 s). It explicitly changes `body.scrollLeft` across the column window while the row flight is active, then performs one/nine left selections. Observation confirms `createViewData` ran with `row.isVdomUpdating=true`, followed by row and covering-body vnode adoption. During the crossing, model/VDOM already named c11 or c3 while the adopted vnode still named c12; the terminal states converge to one selected cell on all four surfaces. That observed crossing alone is therefore insufficient to reproduce the failure. It does not justify porting the text-field reported-value hook from #18914: grid selection classes are engine-owned and cannot be declared current in the vnode unless the corresponding DOM change occurred.

The temporary crossing observer is also archived and removed from the tracked spec. No production fix is claimed. The next candidate-specific check should include Ada's #19513 emitted-root partition, while keeping the relationship to this recurrence a hypothesis until a failing producer is isolated.
